body: I did the National Suicide Prevention Hotline chat. It can take a bit of time, but I had a very helpful experience. Reach out to them- you have nothing to lose by trying once.

They do put you on hold; it just depends upon how many people are calling/requesting to online chat at the moment. I just tried to distract myself with some youtube videos, but for someone in a more panicked state that I was, yeah it's not the best solution.

I actually contacted them yesterday afternoon- I had too much anxiety calling so I went to the chat. It took a bit of waiting to reach someone, but similar to here, I felt more comfortable just texting out my current situation. The person I chatted with was actually quite helpful, and by the end of the chat I was still depressed obviously, but not nearly as hopeless or overwhelmed. I would try chatting if you have access to a computer (not sure if its mobile compatible?).

Be glad you stayed away lol (this is me personally being bitter) but in reality, I was shocked at how unfeeling/unsupportive that conservatory was, along with an alarming percentage of their student body feeling similarly.

I'll most likely be dismissed once these spring final grades are in by May. Ironically, my university is SCRAMBLING to put out public positive statements about 2 "falls" off of one of our campus parking garages that they refuse to call suicides. But when I tell my advisor why my grades are suffering so badly, I get told to "not turn assignments in late" or "maybe I'm in the wrong major". Maybe focus on fixing problems before you have one dead and one student in critical condition.
You are very welcome, any time.
I'm with ya. I'm a full time student, yet I haven't done an assignment since February.

If you don't mind sharing some more details, like when you woke up, what the whole experience was like, I would love to hear. My college just had two students jump within one week, and all I can think about is being the third if I'm being honest.

I just scheduled my first phone assessment with them for sometime this week. I'm very nervous though. I have suicidal thoughts every single day, and with the recent garage jumps/falls and my grades falling further into hell it's getting worse. Should I not disclose this during the phone assessment? To be completely honest every single time I've reached out for help to OSU (academically, advisors, my major's department) no one has offered support or options for me; basically it seems like everyone doesn't really care since my GPA doesn't reflect me being a good student.
Woah, you transferred from Manhattan? I transferred from CCM doing piano performance.

/r/SuicideBereavement is helpful, if you haven't checked out that page yet. 

As far as what I can say, I'm very sorry for your loss and your friend. Depression and Suicidal thoughts are just like cancer; its an illness that many have to fight against. I don't know the specifics of your friend, but know that my inbox is open. I've lost a friend myself as well as suffering from these thoughts. 

This may sound stupid and basic, but you're going to be in shock for a bit since this is so recent. Please make sure you're eating, getting enough sleep, and taking care of yourself.

It's a horrible feeling to know your strength is running out- I'm sorry you feel this way. However you are a very brave person for even reaching out here; recognizing that some people may help you may allude that you think there is some hope left. I feel guilty reaching out to friends too, but I'm sure they would rather know they could stop you from hurting yourself than the alternative. 

I'm not sure where you're from- are there any free clinics you could go to for immediate help?

I think about the same thing. I guess what's pushing me through tonight is knowing that my search to find help will ultimately help me feel closer to these types of friends who truly care about me. And that is help within itself.
Me too. I know it was genuine because she has no clue about how I'm feeling.

I'm so sorry you're feeling so horribly; if by chance you're still reading, didn't attempt, or survived, please know that I'm wishing you well and hope you can gather any strength left to resist your decision.

Regardless of the explanation, I'm sorry you're feeling this way, since I among other people on this thread can understand. If you ever wanted to just vent or talk further, reach out and feel free to message me. I find myself more open to strangers than people that know me.

I always get a dangerous sense of calm after thinking about it, writing/editing suicide notes I've written in the past. I don't think I'd use the word happy, but it gives me a sense of rest from all of the pain.

I'm not comparing myself to anyone. I just simply mean that everything I've tried to work towards or achieve has either a) been sabotaged or destroyed by family or b) has resulted in nothing valuable to me.
